reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown explain Mark's double cock-crow as fuller detail: the other three Gospels report only the final crow that Mark also records.

sides.snippet: Then he began to curse and to swear, \"I don't know the man!\" Immediately the rooster crowed.
sides.verseText: Then he began to curse and to swear, \"I don't know the man!\" Immediately the rooster crowed.

sides.snippet: But he denied it, saying, \"I neither know, nor understand what you are saying.\" He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
sides.verseText: But he denied it, saying, \"I neither know, nor understand what you are saying.\" He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
